appraisal_events.evidence: Saniette leur offrait un souffre-douleur quotidien... on avait soin de l'inviter avec des paroles aimables et persuasives... à seules fins alors de le chatouiller et de lui faire des brimades quand il ne pourra plus s'échapper.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saniette, the target of the cruelty the accepted annotation attributes to the Verdurins, is cajoled into staying within the group only so he can continue to be humiliated; his apparent inclusion is in fact a trap.

appraisal_events.evidence: «Exquis, délicieux, pas pion pour un sou, fantaisiste, léger, ma femme l'adore, moi aussi!» répondit M. Verdurin sur un ton d'exagération... Alors seulement je compris que ce qu'il m'avait dit de Brichot était ironique.
appraisal_events.explanation: M. Verdurin's exaggerated praise of Brichot is revealed by the narrator to be mockery rather than genuine esteem, quietly diminishing Brichot beneath a surface compliment; his emotional handshake of condolence is also met with no response from Verdurin.

appraisal_events.evidence: dans ces milieux bourgeois et artistes où il passait pour l'incarnation même de l'inversion... on le confondait avec un comte Leblois de Charlus... arrêté... dans une descente de police restée fameuse... toutes les histoires qu'on racontait sur Charlus s'appliquaient au faux.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's reputation is badly damaged in the bourgeois and artistic milieu depicted, but the narrator explains this stems from confusion with an unrelated man of the same name, making the local discredit real in social effect yet factually misapplied.

ambiguities: Charlus's bad reputation in bourgeois and artistic circles is attributed by the narrator largely to confusion with an unrelated 'faux Charlus' arrested in a police raid; it is ambiguous how much this constitutes a genuine local diminishment of the baron versus an ironic demonstration of how unreliable such gossip is.

status_effects.explanation: Saniette occupies the designated position of the group's scapegoat, kept close only to be tormented, a clear local loss of standing.
Beneath ostentatious praise, Brichot is quietly mocked by his host, undercutting his local standing even though he remains unaware of it.
Within the bourgeois/artistic milieu of the scene, Charlus's reputation is tarnished, though the narrator frames this as resting on mistaken identity rather than his actual conduct.
